blocks.title: What the server does with a key

nodes.label: App sends POST /charge
nodes.detail: The app makes the key (any random id) before the first try, and sends the same key on every retry of that order.

nodes.label: Look up K1
nodes.detail: A small table: key → state (running or done) and the saved reply. Redis or a DB table with a unique index; entries expire after ≈24 h.

nodes.label: K1 seen?
nodes.detail: Three outcomes: never seen, done (a reply is saved), or running (another request holds the key).

nodes.label: Return saved reply
nodes.detail: The retry gets the first reply back, word for word. The card is not touched.

nodes.label: Claim K1
nodes.detail: Written before any money moves, with insert-if-absent, so two racing requests cannot both claim it.

nodes.label: 409 · try again
nodes.detail: The first request has not finished, so there is nothing to return yet. The app waits a moment and retries with the same key.

nodes.label: Charge the card
nodes.detail: Only the request that claimed K1 reaches this box.

nodes.label: Save reply under K1
nodes.detail: From now on every retry takes the "done" branch.

nodes.label: Reply to the app
nodes.detail: If this reply is lost too, the next retry still lands on "done".

steps.say: The app sends the charge with a key it made: **K1**. A retry reuses the same key.
Before anything else, the server looks K1 up.
Three possible answers: never seen, done, or still running.
Never seen → **claim K1** as running, before touching money.
Charge the card. Only the claimer gets here, so it happens once.
Save the reply under K1, then send it.
A retry after a lost reply finds K1 **done** → same reply, no second charge.
A retry while the first is still running → **409**, try again shortly.

blocks.text: Same key → same answer. **Claim** the key before you charge; **save** the reply after.

blocks.title: One page request, through a CDN

nodes.label: You open the page
nodes.detail: Your browser asks DNS for the site; the CDN answers with the address of the closest edge server.

nodes.label: Nearest edge server
nodes.detail: One of hundreds of CDN machines around the world, each keeping copies of popular files.

nodes.label: Has a copy?
nodes.detail: Copies have a lifetime (cache TTL). A fresh copy is a hit; missing or stale is a miss.

nodes.label: Sent from Mumbai
nodes.detail: A hit: the file never leaves the city. This is most requests on a busy site.

nodes.label: Fetch from origin
nodes.detail: A miss: the edge asks your real server once.

nodes.label: Edge keeps a copy
nodes.detail: The next person in Pune gets the ≈20 ms path.

steps.say: You open the page. DNS points you at the **nearest** CDN server.
That edge server is in Mumbai, not where the site lives.
Does Mumbai already have a fresh copy?
Yes → served from Mumbai in **≈20 ms**.
No → fetched from the origin once, then **kept** for the next visitor.
